rites.name: Veseitheth
rites.text: Veseitheth is the concept of resonance that holds the first roots of Corialor in tune as they condense out of the Singing. It is less a being than a pattern of sustained tone, binding groves and nascent kingdoms to one another across the early Age of the first sovereign.

rites.name: Lialeonus
rites.text: Lialeonus is the concept of the first rooting in Corialor, the note that sounded when the earliest roots pushed through the dark and bound the world together. In the Age of the first sovereign, it is said to guide how groves grow and kingdoms take shape around them.

rites.name: Zephiseizis
rites.text: Zephiseizis is the concept of a sounding that gives shape to the roots of the world, a note held long enough for matter to settle into form. In the Holy Age, priests of flame invoke it at temple thresholds, believing each kindled hearth answers its hum.

rites.name: Grimozhar
rites.text: Grimozhar is a concept of Corialor, a binding-principle that the Courts of the second age used to seal the doors between worlds during the first sovereign's reign. It is said to hold a whole grove's worth of stored oath-force, released only when a trial is answered truthfully.

rites.name: Vanaraum
rites.text: Vanaraum is a concept of Corialor, the principle by which a court's judgment becomes binding on the world, held by the council that built the first doors between worlds. In the Age of Sundering it was invoked to hold landfall together when old bonds began to break.

rites.name: Veneireth
rites.text: Veneireth is the concept of the branching point where Corialor's future splits into three, a moment the Library catalogues as a shelf of outcomes rather than a single road. It is less a force than a hinge, and its acts are felt as the sudden closing of some possibilities and the opening of others.

rites.name: Siliorlys
rites.text: Siliorlys is a concept in Corialor, a quiet abstraction through which the Three Futures are weighed during the Holy Age of flame and temples. It is held to be the principle by which the Library shelves each branching ending, so that no outcome is lost though none is chosen.
